title: A Magpie Looked in a Mirror and Tried to Scratch Off a Mark

scenes.text: A mark on its throat, and a mirror. Most animals fail this test.
Most animals treat a mirror like a rival. These magpies checked the mark and scratched at it with their feet.
Without the mirror, they barely touched the mark at all.
In 2008, it was the first evidence of this kind of self-recognition in a bird.
The researchers say it suggests the ability evolved separately in birds and in mammals.
A bird that knows exactly who is in the mirror.

description:
Researchers put a colored mark on a magpie's throat. Only in front of a mirror did the birds scratch at it.
In 2008, it was reported as the first evidence of mirror self-recognition in a non-mammal.
What do you think the magpie saw?
first_comment: Which animal would you test in a mirror next?
